transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-05 15:00 UTC, duration ~52m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Sana Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE join 2nd half), Diego Marquez (NovaHealth Head of ML), Priya Shah (PM), Liam O'Neill (Security), Sara Gomez (Data Eng)

Summary (auto): quick scoping call to align success criteria for a POC that will evaluate open models for multilingual clinical triage and note-summarization. Focus: quality tradeoffs, latency & cost targets, dataset for benchmarks, and private vs hosted deployment constraints.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining — can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Diego: yeah, Diego from NovaHealth, head of ML, we own the triage pipeline and a lot of clinical extraction.
[00:16] Priya: Priya, PM, running the POC, timeline: want pilot live in staging in 6 weeks.
[00:22] Liam: Liam, security, I'll mainly be on the compliance questions.
[00:25] Sana: Sana from Redwood, I'll run the bench and help pick models and config.
[00:30] Alex: perfect. high level, Priya noted 6 week goal, tell us what success looks like.

[00:45] Priya: product success is twofold — accuracy: we need entity / label F1s comparable to our current internal BERT-CRF baseline (we're at ~0.87 on English triage labels) across English and Spanish, and latency/cost: p50 latency under 150ms and cost per request under $0.03 ideally. If we can hit that in staging we'll greenlight a small pilot.

[01:20] Diego: also quality for free-text summarization - clinical summary length ~3-5 sentences, preserve key findings and red-flag symptoms. We have a golden set for evaluation.

[01:35] Sana: sounds reasonable. quick clarification — is the Spanish traffic single-country LATAM Spanish plus Portuguese?
[01:40] Priya: mostly Spain and Mexico, and ~10% Portuguese (Brazil). So multilingual but skewed to en/es.

[02:05] Alex: ok good. talking models — we proposed an open-model shortlist. any hard requirements on license?
[02:12] Diego: must be commercially usable; no restrictions for production.

[02:20] Sana: shortlist we're thinking: Llama-2-Chat 13B (instruction-tuned), Mistral-7B-Instruct, and Falcon-40B-Instruct as a higher-quality baseline — all quantizable. we also discussed a smaller distilled model for edge cost constraints, and optionally testing newer Llama3 variants if licensing checks out.

[02:55] Priya: can you say tradeoffs? like which model is best for Spanish and clinical vocabulary?

[03:05] Sana: sure — quick, rough notes: Llama-2-chat 13B: strong instruction tuning, solid general language, good instruction-following but slightly weaker on specialized medical expressions unless we finetune. Mistral-7B-Instruct: fast, cost-efficient, surprisingly good multilingual transfer for es/pt when used with prompt engineering. Falcon-40B-Instruct: biggest quality wins, especially for complex summarization and nuanced clinical phrasing, but higher latency/cost, and needs more memory; quantization to 8-bit or 4-bit affects quality differently.

[03:45] Diego: we probably need to test domain adapter vs full finetune. we don't want to retrain large models from scratch.

[03:55] Sana: agreed — recommended path: 1) baseline zero-shot/instruct eval on your golden set, 2) test lightweight LoRA/adapters, 3) only go to full fine-tune if necessary. adapters often close a lot of gap at much lower cost.

[04:20] Liam: security question — for POC data, can we keep everything in our VPC or do we need to send data to hosted?
[04:28] Alex: Redwood offers three modes — Hosted API for fast iteration, Dedicated reserved capacity for consistent throughput, and Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for isolated processing. For POC, recommended: run initial bench on Redwood Hosted with strong retention and encryption, then move to Dedicated or Private depending on security sign-off. We can also do an on-prem snapshot for a limited bench.

[04:58] Liam: do you support customer-managed KMS?
[05:02] Sana: yes, KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated; Hosted has server-side encryption with SOC2 controls. We'll share the security brief.

[05:20] Priya: about benchmarks — what metrics will Redwood run by default?

[05:25] Sana: we'll run: quality (F1, BLEU/ROUGE for summaries, hallucination checks with QA pairs), latency (p50,p95), throughput/QPS, and cost per 1k tokens. Also tokenization mismatch checks since your data has a lot of numeric values and ICD codes.

[06:00] Diego: important: entity labeling is sensitive, we need PII redaction before inference. can Redwood do a preprocessor?

[06:10] Sana: yes we can run a sanitized pipeline — we usually recommend local pre-redaction or token-level masking before sending to Hosted. For Dedicated/Private it can be done within the customer's VPC.

[06:35] Alex: on workload sizing — Diego, can you walk us through expected traffic and concurrency for the pilot vs prod?

[06:42] Diego: pilot stage: ~200-500 reqs/day, peak concurrency ~5-10. Production target next quarter is 2k qps peak for triage service during business hours — that's the big jump. For the POC though, we just need representative latency and small-scale throughput (~20 qps).

[07:12] Sana: great — bench hardware options: we'll run the three models on Dedicated instance shapes that mimic your prod target (NVIDIA A100 80GB for Falcon-40B, and 1-2 A10/A100s for 13B/Mistral). We'll also profile cheaper shapes for cost projections.

[07:40] Priya: timeline check — you said share benchmark plan and prompts by next week?

[07:44] Alex: yes, we'll send a benchmark matrix and ask NovaHealth to provide gold-set and sample traffic. then bench + shared results in ~7 business days after we have data. so aligns with your 6 week staging goal if no blockers.

[08:05] Diego: about multilingual evals — should we include translation step or use the model natively?

[08:12] Sana: prefer native multilingual evals first. models differ: Mistral often needs prompting tweaks, Llama2 and Falcon have broader multilingual capacity. Also consider a hybrid route: use small translation step for Portuguese if quality falls off. We'll include both approaches in the bench matrix.

[08:45] Priya: what's a realistic expectation for hallucination/harm mitigation for clinical summaries?

[08:50] Sana: with instruction-tuned models + prompt guardrails and QA pairs we can reduce hallucination, but not eliminate it. We'll measure answer faithfulness against the golden QA set; target is under 5% critical hallucination on triage labels. If above threshold we recommend fallback policy to the baseline model or human review for edge cases.

[09:18] Liam: we need audit logs and traceability — can Redwood provide per-request logs in Private/Dedicated with redacted content?

[09:25] Alex: yes, per-request metadata, token-level cost, and hash-based request ids can be stored. actual content can be redacted or hashed depending on your policy. We'll include examples in the security doc.

[09:45] Jordan (joined): hey all, briefly — for benching I'll instrument KV cache and prefix cache to simulate real sessions; often that shows large cost savings for triage where many requests share prefixes. Note: transcripts occasionally call it the K-V cash haha.

[10:15] Diego: good, caching could be huge for repeated triage templates.

[10:30] Priya: budget question — if we hit quality targets, what are rough monthly costs at 2k qps?

[10:38] Sana: rough thumb: Falcon-40B at production scale without aggressive quantization could be several 10s of thousands per month; Llama2-13B or Mistral-7B with 4-bit quantization and batching can be an order of magnitude cheaper. We'll provide a cost curve in the matrix (latency vs cost vs quality).

[11:05] Diego: do you support mixed-routing? e.g., high-quality model for edge cases, cheaper model for bulk?

[11:10] Alex: yes — Redwood supports smart routing and fallback policies: route by confidence threshold, request metadata, or cost budget. We can prototype a two-model routing policy in the POC.

[11:33] Priya: any required dataset format?

[11:36] Sara: we'll provide JSONL with fields: id, language, text, labels, anonymized_patient_flag. Is that ok?

[11:41] Sana: perfect. include your golden set and we will keep a locked eval script.

[12:00] Diego: about evaluation metrics — we'll prioritize F1 for labels, and ROUGE-L for summaries plus a clinical-accuracy score we calculate.

[12:10] Sana: we'll run per-lang breakdowns and delta vs your baseline; also speed and token-cost breakdowns.

[12:25] Priya: would you do live demo of bench results or just a report?

[12:30] Alex: both. we'll send the matrix and then schedule a 30m walkthrough to interpret results — propose 2025-11-13 for results review.

[12:45] Liam: compliance sign-off path — we'll need a written attestation for data residency during POC and an architecture diagram.

[12:52] Alex: we'll include that in the security pack and include options for VPC egress controls.

[13:10] Diego: small nit: in prior email you mentioned Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching — would that be applicable here?

[13:16] Sana: yes, Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and cache windows to meet latency/cost tradeoffs; we'll include those parameter suggestions with expected impact.

[13:35] Priya: ok let's recap and assign owners.

[13:40] Alex: recap: Redwood will produce benchmark plan, sample prompt set, and initial pricing + security brief (Alex/Sana). NovaHealth will send data (Diego/Priya/Sara). Bench to be run by Sana, results and walkthrough on 2025-11-13. Action items and dates in the follow-up email.

[14:05] Diego: thanks — excited to see whether we can get near baseline quality with lighter models; cost is big driver for us.

[14:12] Alex: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the matrix, and Sana will kick off the bench once we have data.

[14:20] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: some words mis-transcribed (Falcon sometimes shown as "Falcony"; K-V cache shown as "K-V cash"), speaker overlaps and short crosstalk present.
